memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: When the woman saw that the fruit of the tree was good for food and pleasing to the eye, and also desirable for gaining wisdom, she took some and ate it. She also gave some to her husband, who was with her, and he ate it. — Gen 3:6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here it is — the single moment that changed everything. And notice how ordinary it looks. There is no dramatic scene, no clap of thunder. Just a look, a reach, and a bite.

See how temptation worked on Eve's heart. The fruit was "good for food" — an appeal to her appetite. It was "pleasing to the eye" — an appeal to her desires. It was "desirable for gaining wisdom" — an appeal to her pride. Centuries later, John describes temptation in almost the same three ways (1 Jn 2:16). The enemy's playbook has hardly changed. What God had forbidden now looked good, beautiful, and wise — and so she took it.

We should not miss that Adam "was with her." This was not only Eve's failure. Adam stood by, silent, and then ate too. Sin entered our world through both of them, and through Adam its shadow fell across us all (Rom 5:12).

Dear friend, if the story ended here, we would be without hope. But God had a plan already in place. Where the first Adam took and brought death, the last Adam, Jesus, gave Himself and brings life (Rom 5:19). At another tree — the cross — He undid what was done at this one. The moment everything broke was not the end of the story.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Which appeal tends to draw you most — appetite, desire, or pride?
2. Where have you stayed silent, like Adam, when you should have spoken or acted?
3. How does the obedience of Christ give you hope in your own struggle with sin?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, I confess that sin still looks appealing to my heart far too often. Thank You that where Adam failed, Jesus obeyed perfectly and gave His life to rescue me. Help me to treasure Christ more than the fleeting pleasures of sin. Amen.
